bib.title: GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic Sharding

read.skipped: References skimmed only; appendix A.4 tail (convolution halo details) read lightly

question: How can a giant sparsely-gated MoE Transformer be trained efficiently on thousands of accelerators with minimal model-code changes, and does it improve massively multilingual translation?
hypothesis: Conditional computation (sparsely-gated MoE) scales quality with sublinear compute cost, beating dense scaling on training efficiency and quality.
contributions: GShard: lightweight sharding annotation APIs (replicate, split, shard) plus an XLA SPMD partitioner with near-constant compilation time
Top-2 gated MoE Transformer with expert capacity, local group dispatching, auxiliary loss and random routing
600B-parameter multilingual NMT model trained in 4 days on 2048 TPU v3 cores
Analysis of depth vs experts, capacity bottleneck, positive transfer and training efficiency

method.summary: Replaces every other Transformer feed-forward layer with a top-2 gated Position-wise MoE layer, one expert per device, and partitions it via GShard annotations and an XLA SPMD partitioner. Six MoE models (128/512/2048 experts, 12/36 layers) are trained on 100-to-English translation and compared with 100 bilingual baselines and a dense 96-layer GPipe Transformer.
method.task: multilingual neural machine translation, 100 languages to English

datasets.name: In-house web-mined parallel corpus, 100 languages to and from English
datasets.size: 25 billion training examples total; approximately 13 billion for the 100-to-English direction
datasets.source: mined from the web [47]; in-house, power-law language imbalance from billions to tens of thousands of examples
datasets.preprocessing: SentencePiece; Kazakh and Latin to English excluded from evaluation

models.name: MoE(2048E,36L)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer, MoE in every other FFN, top-2 gating

other.note: numerical stability issues; results not reported

models.name: T(96L)
models.architecture: dense Transformer encoder-decoder trained with GPipe

models.name: Bilingual baselines
models.architecture: Transformer-Big or Transformer-Base per language pair, batch size and dropout tuned

training.objective: negative log-likelihood plus k * auxiliary load-balancing loss (L = l_nll + k*l_aux); k value not stated
training.optimizer: Adafactor, factored second moment, beta1 = 0.0, beta2 = 0.99 with 1 - t^-0.8 schedule, update clipping 1.0
training.lr_schedule: square root decay after 10k training steps
training.batch_size: 4M tokens for 2048-core models, 1M tokens for 128/512-core models (Table 3)
training.steps: 250k training steps for the 600B model; 0.72 steps/s
training.tokens: 1 trillion tokens per model (checkpoint used for evaluation)
training.precision: float32 weights and activations (bfloat16 tried for 1T, unstable)
training.regularisation: expert capacity limit, random routing of 2nd expert, auxiliary loss
training.hardware: TPU v3; cores equal experts per layer (128, 512, 2048)

inference.decoding: beam search with length normalization, flat beam (beams flattened into one sequence)

other.inference_cluster: same number of devices as training

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: BLEU per language pair on held-out test set; averaged over 100 languages

metrics.name: Delta BLEU
metrics.definition: gain of the multilingual model over the bilingual baseline for that language

metrics.name: TPU v3 core-years
metrics.definition: number of cores times wall-clock time in years

eval.protocol: Single run per configuration, no seeds or significance tests stated; trendlines smoothed with window of 10

limits: Single in-house web-scale dataset and one task (X-to-English MT); not released, so not reproducible
One run per configuration, no seeds or significance tests
Dense baseline T(96L) is a different, deeper architecture with different cost; comparison confounds depth and sparsity
1T-parameter model results omitted due to instability
Authors concede deep-dense models transfer better to low-resource languages than shallow MoE
Sharding assignment uses iterative dataflow heuristics; better assignment left as future work
Capacity per expert must be at least 1, so the O(1/D) capacity scheme cannot scale indefinitely
Hyperparameters k (aux loss), warmup, beam size, sequence length not stated

terms.definition: a uniform threshold on the number of tokens processed by one expert, O(N/E); overflowed tokens pass through residual connections
a compiler transformation that generates a single program to run on all devices, keeping compilation time constant
